incbot: :rotating_light: Paging on-call: elevated 5xx and backpressure on smart-routing service in eu-west (Alert: SR-7211). Start 2004567890

alice (oncall-eng): I’m on it. seeing spike in 5xx from router-proxy -> kv cache timeouts.

bob (sre): copying logs, looks like burst of heavy gen requests + model x-large fallback causing lots of KV churn.

carol (runtime): confirmed. tail of router-proxy: `ERR kv:get timeout 200ms` repeatedly, and continuous batching queue growing.

alice (oncall-eng): impact: some customers hitting degraded latency and errors; premium tenants reporting failures. erin, can you surface any high-priority customer tickets?

erin (support): pulling tickets now. seeing 3 enterprise incidents in eu-west: conv.ai, docsummarize. Notifying CSE.

alice (oncall-eng): mitigation plan: 1) protect host by enabling short-term global rate limit on gen routes 2) steer new requests to cheaper/regional lanes 3) disable x-large fallback for eu-west 4) increase KV client timeouts as a stopgap.

bob (sre): +1. I'll push rate limit now: `rbctl policy apply --cluster eu-west --policy rate-limit-gen=150rps`

mike (deploy-bot): deploy triggered: `policy-service v2.9.1 -> eu-west` started (2004567955).

carol (runtime): doing routing steer: updating smart-routing weights to favor tier-2 and regional fallback to eu-central. patch config:

```
# smart-routing patch
- match: region: eu-west
  action: rebalance
  weights:
    tier-1: 0.4
    tier-2: 0.5
    economy: 0.1
  prefer_region: eu-central
```

alice (oncall-eng): good. also temporarily remove `x-large-quant` as fallback in eu-west: `rbctl model update --region eu-west --fallbacks remove x-large-quant`

carol (runtime): done (2004568020). fallback removed. redispatching queued requests to tier-2.

bob (sre): bumped KV client timeout to 500ms in router-proxy (hotpatch) — config applied (2004568035).

alice (oncall-eng): rate limit and steer live?

bob (sre): yes. saw 60% drop in 5xx in last 30s. latency still elevated but recovering.

erin (support): telling impacted customers we’ve applied mitigations and are routing traffic away from eu-west to reduce errors.

dave (product): what’s the customer-visible tradeoff? increased tail latency or lower quality for some requests?

carol (runtime): some requests will hit smaller model variants (tier-2/economy) — slight quality delta for long-context gen only. latency overall better than erroring.

alice (oncall-eng): next steps: 1) monitor for 10m window 2) if stable, gradually restore fallback after KV tuning 3) run retrospective and add auto-steer rule for sudden percent-of-xlarge failures.

bob (sre): adding temporary quota reductions for non-critical workloads to preserve capacity: `rbctl quota set --scope nonprod --region eu-west --limit 0.2x` (2004568120).

erin (support): sent customer note updates. one asks for ETA for full restore — told them we expect gradual restore in 30-60m pending stability.

alice (oncall-eng): monitoring dashboards: 5xx down from 22% -> 6% since mitigation. batching queue length normalized.

mike (deploy-bot): canary traffic test to eu-west small workload passed (2004568180).

carol (runtime): reenable x-large fallback in a controlled canary only after KV client metrics show steady 5m with error rate <1% and median latency <200ms.

dave (product): please capture customer impact summary for postmortem and customer comms.

alice (oncall-eng): will file incident afterwards. good work. marking incident as mitigated for now, leave thread open for follow-ups. :thumbsup:

alice (oncall-eng): final note: ops-runbook action item — add auto-ratecap-and-steer when x-large fallback error rate >5% for 60s.

erin (support): closing tickets with interim note, will reopen if customers still impacted.

carol (runtime): follow-up checks scheduled: KV cluster health, kernel upgrades on hosts, routing policy safety thresholds.
